thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT PD-7890 fired: GPU_MEMORY_PRESSURE on pool=dedicated-eu-2 (severity=high). sample_rate=1.0

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident created: PD-7890 (GPU memory pressure) — escalated to on-call.

sandeep: acked PD-7890. I'm on it. any customer impact reported?

maria: seeing elevated OOMs in k8s logs for model-serving pods in eu-2, ~4 nodes affected, maybe spillover from a larger batch job.

devon: logs show repeated CUDA allocation failures around same time: `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY`. Putting a quick snippet below.

```
2026-03-14T16:02:12Z model-server-57f8 WARN kernel: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
2026-03-14T16:02:13Z model-server-3a2c ERROR runtime: KV cache eviction spike, evictions=1249
2026-03-14T16:02:14Z model-server-8b1d ERROR inference: failed to allocate 256MB for activation
```

lia: nvidia-smi from one affected node (eu-2-gpu-45):

```
Tue Mar 14 16:01:58 2026
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 525.89.02    Driver Version: 525.89.02    CUDA Version: 12.1 |
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. |
|  0  A100-SXM4-40GB   Off        | 00000000:65:00.0 Off |                  0 |
+-------------------------------+-----------------------------------------------+
|  0  40C    P0    60W / 400W |   39715MiB / 40960MiB |   1795MiB MIG  |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

maria: so memory is near-saturation (39.7GB/40GB) and KV cache evictions are spiking. Could be a combination of a recent canary with larger context lengths + prefix cache blowup.

sandeep: timeline: alerts started 16:01. We had an autoscale event earlier at 15:58 for a spike in requests; maybe the scaler packed pods onto fewer nodes. devon, can you check cluster-scheduler events?

devon: looking... `kubectl describe node eu-2-gpu-45` shows pods evicted last hour and a recent daemon that set `accelerator=dedicated` affinities. I see a new canary deployment `rl-chat-v2` with `max_seq_len: 4096` rolled at 15:50.

lia: can we temporarily route traffic for dedicated-eu-2 to fallback model (smaller quantized) for customer-affecting routes? ops runbook step suggests `redwood route override` command.

sandeep: yes. I'll flip fallback for affected customer groups. Doing safe fallback for route: `redwood routes set --pool dedicated-eu-2 --route /chat --model rwd-quant-3b --reason "OOM mitigation"`

incident-bot: action executed: route override queued (run id run-9922).

maria: meanwhile let's cordon the suspect node to avoid new pods scheduling and drain low-priority pods from it. sandeep, want me to run drain?

sandeep: please. Use `kubectl drain eu-2-gpu-45 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data` and keep one warm pod pinned for debugging.

devon: running drain now — will evict non-critical pods. ETA ~90s.

(90s later)

devon: drain complete, low-priority pods evicted. One debug pod kept for repro. Kernel logs still show intermittent CUDA alloc failures but frequency decreased.

lia: customer impact check — telemetry indicates increased 5xx rate for three dedicated customers, most requests showed `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` token. I'm opening support tickets for `acme-inc` and `olympus-ai`. No public pages yet.

sandeep: good. Set status: investigating, and add note: "fallback to rwd-quant-3b for dedicated-eu-2 for mitigation".

maria: also lowering batch size on the canary by env var `MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=1024` to reduce peak allocs. Pushing config now.

incident-bot: config change applied to deployment rl-chat-v2-canary (replicas=2).

devon: KV cache metrics: prefix cache hit dropped 8% but eviction rate fell 70% after drain + fallback.

lia: nudge to SRE: recommend scaling node pool by +2 GPUs temporarily (eu-2) to reduce pressure while canary is validated. Who can authorize?

sandeep: I can approve autoscaling up in the short term. Initiating scale: `infra scale-gpu-pool eu-2 +2 --reason "OOM mitigation"`

pagerduty-bot: PD-7890 acknowledged by sandeep at 2026-03-14T16:03:05Z.

(10m later)

devon: autoscale completed, 2 nodes added. Memory pressure normalized across pool, OOMs dropped to baseline.

maria: rolling back the route override after we confirm stability? or keep until canary config validated?

sandeep: keep override for 30m and monitor. If stable, we'll revert. Also capture heap traces from debug pod and attach to PD.

lia: attaching logs and timeline to PD-7890. Customer tickets opened. Notifying support to email affected accounts.

incident-bot: PD-7890 updated: mitigation in place (route override + node scale + canary batch-size reduction). Status: monitoring.

sandeep: thanks all. I'll handoff to morning on-call at 17:00. If anyone sees a regression, ping me and escalate PD.

maria: noted. good catch on the long context canary. we should add a preflight check for context-length vs pool mem.

devon: will file follow-up action item in eng-runtime: "context-length preflight + autoscaler guardrails".

lia: last check (16:17): 5xx rate trending back to normal. closing immediate mitigation.

pagerduty-bot: PD-7890 status changed to "resolved" by sandeep at 2026-03-14T16:18:00Z (note: monitoring for 30m).

sandeep: resolving thread here. follow-ups: postmortem + runbook update. :white_check_mark:
